description: Offers a comprehensive review of computer systems by bridging computer architecture, processor design, and operating systems principles essential for high-performance computing.
learning_objectives: Understand computer organization, instruction set architectures, and assembly language programming.
Analyze CPU datapath, hardwired and microprogrammed control unit designs, pipelining, and memory hierarchy.
Master operating system core services including process management, CPU scheduling, concurrency, and deadlock handling.
Examine virtual memory management, file systems, disk scheduling, and I/O system architectures.
outline: Computer Architecture & ISA: Performance measures, memory locations/operations, addressing modes, instruction sets, machine and assembly language programs.
Processing Unit Design: Registers, datapath, CPU instruction cycle, micro-operations, bus architectures, interrupt handling.
Control Unit & Pipelining: Hardwired control unit design, microprogrammed control unit, instruction pipelining, pipeline hazards, branch prediction.
Memory Hierarchy: Cache memory mapping, cache coherence, virtual memory, paging, segmentation, page replacement policies.
Process Management & Synchronization: Process lifecycle, threads, CPU scheduling algorithms, critical section problem, semaphores, mutexes, monitors.
Deadlocks & Storage Systems: Deadlock characterization, prevention, avoidance (Banker's algorithm), detection, disk scheduling, file system implementation.
Lab Component: Linux shell programming, POSIX system calls, multi-threaded programming, and architecture simulation.
